text: Thank you for the ECG request; while I await those results, did you experience any palpitations, dizziness, or sweating immediately before fainting? Additionally, how long were you unconscious, and did you have any injuries from the fall?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Commotio Cordis secondary to micturition syncope. The timing immediately after urination suggests a sudden drop in blood pressure (vasovagal response), but the lack of cardiac history combined with the specific "post-micturition" trigger makes pure syncope more likely than a primary arrhythmia, though the ECG results are crucial to rule out underlying structural heart disease or long QT syndrome which can be unmasked by such stressors. Given the short duration of unconsciousness (30 seconds) and rapid recovery without confusion, this leans heavily toward a benign reflex event, but we must confirm the cardiac status before discharge. Did you have any chest pain or shortness of breath during the event? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram to rule out structural abnormalities.
